brief: JPMorgan's September 18 international morning briefing rounds up a busy central bank week. Oil and rates extended their move lower on reports China urged Iran to rein in the Houthis and Iran got UN-meeting visas, supporting a tech-led equity rally led by NDX over EU. The BOE held as expected but is geared toward a hike, with JPM's economist now seeing another move in February. Its QT plan cuts gilt APF holdings to zero and routes sales to the DMO. The BOJ hiked 25bp with a dovish-skewed dissent, weakening the yen (USDJPY above 157) and lifting Japanese equities. EU-China trade tension continues ahead of an October 8 Beijing visit and next week's Trump-Xi summit. JPM stays tactically cautious/neutral on global equities, long US and Asia versus Europe, and is now adding cheap EU index hedges to prior since-May bullishness. Separately, JPM's positioning desk reports a quiet, neutral HF tape but bearish ETF flows and stretched CTA extremes in crude and US bonds, and its EM desk stays bullish, long China H-shares, KWEB, Taiwan and a long-India/short-ASEA pair.
